gsp.scheme: EU GSP (Standard GSP) - Regulation (EU) 978/2012 to 31 Dec 2026; Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 applies from 1 Jan 2027
gsp.notes: India is a Standard GSP beneficiary, but for 1 Jan 2026-31 Dec 2028 GSP preferences are suspended for Indian goods in sections S-5 (mineral products), S-6a (chemicals), S-7a (plastics), S-7b (rubber), S-11a (textile materials), S-13 (stone/ceramic/glass), S-14 (pearls/precious metals), S-15a (iron and steel), S-15b (other base metals), S-16 (machinery/electrical), S-17a (railway), S-17b (motor vehicles, aircraft, ships) under Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1909. Apparel (S-11b), leather/footwear and most food sections are NOT in the graduated list. The new GSP Regulation (EU) 2026/1395 applies from 1 Jan 2027; per the Commission Q&A India keeps Standard GSP for two years after the EU-India FTA starts to apply. Proof: REX statement on origin.

origin_proof.preferential_document: Statement on origin (REX) for EU GSP; text per Annex 22-07 UCC-IA, on invoice or other commercial document
origin_proof.issued_by: Exporter self-certifies. Registration in REX needed when a consignment's originating content exceeds EUR 6,000; REX number obtained via EU REX pre-application and approval by an Indian competent authority
origin_proof.how: Register once via the EU REX pre-application portal, which an Indian competent authority (designated under DGFT notification 51/2016, e.g. Export Inspection Council) validates; then type the Annex 22-07 statement on origin with REX number on the invoice for each shipment. No GSP claim possible for goods in India's graduated sections. The EU-India FTA statement on origin is NOT usable until that FTA enters into force.

CBAM definitive regime from 1 Jan 2026: EU importers of iron/steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity must be authorised and surrender CBAM certificates; Indian engineering/metal exporters must supply embedded-emissions data.

REACH: chemical substances (incl. in dyes, inks, cosmetics ingredients and some articles such as textiles/leather) must be registered by the EU manufacturer/importer or an Only Representative; restricted substances (e.g. azo dyes, Cr(VI) in leather) apply.
Cosmetics need an EU Responsible Person, product safety report and CPNP notification under Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 before sale.
